description:
“Every piece we leave in space is a monument to human curiosity. 'The Human Archive,' looking back from the year 2126, transforms seemingly forgotten space remnants into an interactive museum of memory.

 Because being abandoned does not mean being forgotten." 

We want to This present this to students in a fun, game-like way.
summary:
THE HUMAN ARCHIVE: TERK EDİLMİŞ ≠ UNUTULMUŞ

Peki ya uzayda bıraktığımız izler, geleceğin arkeolojik keşiflerine dönüşürse?

THE HUMAN ARCHIVE, kullanıcıların uzay arkeologlarına dönüştüğü ve insanlığın uzay görevlerinden geriye kalan unutulmuş izleri keşfettiği, 2126 yılında geçen etkileşimli bir dijital deneyimdir. Kullanıcılar, sürükleyici bir arşiv aracılığıyla Ay’da, Mars’ta ve uzayın derinliklerinde bırakılmış gerçek uzay araçlarını, gezgin robotları, bilimsel cihazları ve diğer nesneleri keşfeder.

Projemiz, geçmiş uzay donanımlarını ve görev verilerini özellikle genç kitleler için erişilebilir, ilgi çekici ve anlamlı hâle getirme sorununa çözüm sunmayı amaçlıyor. Doğrulanmış NASA bilgilerini, etkileşimli keşfi, görsel hikâye anlatımını ve gizem odaklı bir senaryoyu bir araya getirerek bilimsel kayıtları bir keşif yolculuğuna dönüştürüyoruz.

THE HUMAN ARCHIVE, terk edilmiş olmanın unutulmuş olmak anlamına gelmediğini hatırlatıyor. Uzayda bıraktığımız her nesne; insan merakının, yenilikçiliğinin ve tarihinin bir parçasını taşıyor. Bu izleri korumak, gelecek nesillerin yalnızca neler başardığımızı değil, nasıl bir insanlık olduğumuzu da anlamasına yardımcı oluyor.
details:
THE HUMAN ARCHIVE — Project Details

What does the project do and how does it work?

THE HUMAN ARCHIVE is an interactive digital archive experience that transforms users into space archaeologists living in the year 2126. Our project focuses on rediscovering spacecraft, scientific equipment, and historical traces left behind by humanity’s exploration of the Moon, Mars, and deep space.

Users begin their journey by accessing the terminal of an abandoned space station in the future. They explore archive records related to lunar, Martian, and other space missions, follow clues, discover objects, and learn about the scientific data and stories behind each discovery.

Each archive entry follows an engaging storytelling structure designed to make the exploration process more immersive: first, a clue; then, the discovered object; followed by verified NASA data and a story explaining its historical significance. Users can also add their own thoughts and messages to the final section of the archive, turning the experience into a personal journey of discovery.

What are the benefits of the project?

When space missions come to an end, the spacecraft and equipment left behind are often viewed merely as technical records. However, these objects represent humanity’s scientific progress, curiosity, failures, and passion for exploration.

THE HUMAN ARCHIVE aims to make this information more accessible and engaging, especially for young people and students. By combining verified NASA mission data with interactive exploration and storytelling, our project allows users not just to read scientific information, but to experience it.

What is the intended impact of the project?

Our goal is to ensure that future generations do not view space exploration solely through the lens of successful missions. The end of a mission does not mean the end of its scientific or historical value. Even abandoned space equipment can contain valuable information for future research, engineering projects, and new discoveries.

Our project aims to inspire curiosity about space science among young people, encourage the habit of researching scientific data, and create historical awareness of humanity’s presence and legacy in space.

How creative is our project, and what factors did our team consider?

The creative aspect of our project lies in combining real space missions with a futuristic space archaeology scenario. Instead of presenting users with a traditional information catalogue, we place them in the role of a researcher in the year 2126, looking back into humanity’s past.

The concept “ABANDONED ≠ FORGOTTEN” represents the central idea of our project. By bringing scientific accuracy and emotional storytelling together, we aim to highlight the human effort and stories of exploration behind every object.

Throughout the development process, our team considered several important factors, including scientific accuracy, the reliability of NASA sources, user experience, accessibility for different age groups, visual consistency, and compatibility with mobile devices. We also made sure that verified information provided by NASA could be clearly distinguished from the storytelling and visual interpretations created by our team.

The central message of THE HUMAN ARCHIVE is simple:

Every trace we leave in space is part of humanity’s shared history. They may be abandoned, but they are not forgotten.


Here is the complete list of tools, technologies, software, and hardware I used to develop THE HUMAN ARCHIVE.

1. Code Editor

  • Visual Studio Code (VS Code)

2. Programming Languages

  • HTML5 — Used for the website’s structure and content.
  • CSS3 — Used for styling, layouts, animations, and responsive design.
  • Vanilla JavaScript — Used to develop interactive features, navigation, discovery systems, timelines, progress tracking, and user interactions.

3. AI Assistance

  • ChatGPT — Used for brainstorming, development guidance, code assistance, troubleshooting, and refining ideas.

4. Development and Version Control

  • Git — Used for version control.
  • GitHub — Used for repository hosting and project management.
  • GitHub Pages — Used to deploy and host the website.

5. Browser Technologies and APIs

  • localStorage — Used to save user progress and personal archive data locally.
  • HTML5 Canvas API — Used for the interactive drawing feature.
  • HTML Audio API and Web Audio API — Used for sound effects and audio interactions.

6. Digital Assets and Media

  • WebP — Used for optimized images.
  • MP3 — Used for background ambience, sound effects, and audio cues.

7. Testing

  • Google Chrome — Used for browser testing and verifying the website’s functionality and responsiveness.

8. Hardware

  • A standard Windows laptop/computer.
  • No specialized hardware or external physical devices were used.
